title: Dispute over credibility of Gaza Health Ministry casualty figures
body:
On 27 October 2023, the Gaza Health Ministry reported at least 7,326 Palestinians killed and more than 18,000 wounded since the start of the war. The ministry draws on hospital and morgue data and had released a 212-page document listing the names and identity numbers of the dead. Israel reported that more than 1,400 people had been killed in the Hamas attack on 7 October at that time.

The same day, the head of the UN agency for Palestinian refugees, Philippe Lazzarini, told reporters in Jerusalem that the ministry's figures had long been regarded as reliable. He said the figures were considered credible and that no one had ever really challenged them in previous conflicts. The World Health Organization's Michael Ryan said the numbers largely reflect the level of death and injury, though they may not be exact on a minute-by-minute basis.

The credibility of the ministry became a political issue. US President Joe Biden said he had no notion that the Palestinians were telling the truth about how many people had been killed. US National Security Council spokesperson John Kirby described the ministry as a front for Hamas, although a report by the Huffington Post found the State Department had consistently relied on its figures. The ministry also revised its initial toll for the Al-Ahli Arab Hospital explosion from about 500 to 471. Critics, including some public health experts, argued that disputing the numbers dehumanised Palestinians.
